question: The most common route for MNC investment is to buy up ________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**local companies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Multinational Corporations (MNCs) commonly invest in **local companies** as it provides a quick entry into the market.
 
• Acquiring local companies helps MNCs leverage existing **infrastructure, networks, and brand recognition** of the acquired firms.
 
• This route allows MNCs to overcome **regulatory barriers** and gain access to the local market’s customer base more efficiently.
 
• Mergers and acquisitions of local companies enable MNCs to obtain **local expertise and skilled human resources**, which are crucial for navigating regional market dynamics.
 
• Examples include Facebook’s acquisition of Indian startup Meesho and Walmart’s acquisition of Flipkart, signaling strategic investment in local companies to strengthen their foothold in emerging markets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Multinational Corporations (MNCs)**

 
 
• MNCs are companies that operate in multiple countries but are headquartered in one specific country.
 
• They play a significant role in global trade and often influence economic policies in host countries.
 
• Examples include Apple, Amazon, Google, Unilever, and Toyota.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of Acquiring Local Companies**
 
 
• Facilitates market entry by utilizing the existing customer base and brand loyalty.
 
• Helps in adapting to **local culture and consumer preferences**.
 
• Reduces operational risks by leveraging local expertise and infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Challenges Faced by MNCs in Local Investments**
 
 
• Regulatory and legal hurdles in host countries.
 
• Integration challenges between the MNC and the acquired company due to differences in corporate culture.
 
• Potential backlash from local communities or governments against foreign ownership.
 
 
 
• **Alternative Routes for MNC Investment**
 
 
• Establishing wholly-owned subsidiaries in the host country.
 
• Entering joint ventures with local partners to share risks and resources.
 
• Developing strategic alliances to leverage complementary strengths without ownership changes.
